# State Management Checklist: Pilot Evidence Surfaces

**Purpose**: Validate that SPEC-009E requirements fully define read-only task evidence state derivation, state vocabulary, precedence, and UI state boundaries.
**Created**: 2026-05-20
**Feature**: specs/009e-pilot-evidence-surfaces/spec.md

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are stored-evidence-only derivation requirements defined for every v1 response section (`task`, `pilot_eligibility`, `identity`, `packet_artifacts`, `smoke`, `current_stage`, `warnings`, `deferrals`, `source_map`)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define which v1 evidence states are valid for each response section, including available, missing, stale, incomplete, not eligible, redacted, quarantined, superseded, unavailable, and deferred? [Resolved] [Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-035, Data Model §V1 Evidence State Model]
  - Evidence: `data-model.md` §V1 Evidence State Model now defines allowed states and a section-by-section matrix for every v1 response section; `spec.md` FR-035 makes that model authoritative.
- [x] CHK003 Are no-write requirements complete for server-side and client-side paths, including no task mutation, no artifact mutation, no packet generation, no hidden refresh, and no local override state? [Resolved] [Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-022, Spec §FR-024, Spec §FR-036, Plan §Read-Only State Management Constraints]
  - Evidence: `spec.md` FR-036 and `plan.md` §Read-Only State Management Constraints now prohibit server persistence, mutation, hidden refresh, repair/backfill jobs, audit/event writes, and client-side persisted evidence overrides.
- [ ] CHK004 Are archived or cleaned UAT row states specified separately from current active Mission Control state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the meaning of `not_eligible` distinct from `missing`, `incomplete`, and `no_stored_evidence` in requirements text? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK006 Is `stale` defined as a stored-source relationship rather than a time-based refresh trigger? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK007 Are redacted, quarantined, unsafe, and secret-bearing states described with explicit safe-output limits? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK008 Are deferred future-state labels required to remain informational, with no implied runtime authority or control state? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-024]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Are state names consistent across spec, data model, and OpenAPI contract, including snake_case spelling and absence of extra UI-only state aliases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK010 Do section-level state requirements align with HTTP behavior, so incomplete/missing evidence remains a `200` domain state while auth/scope errors remain boundary errors? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK011 Do source precedence rules consistently prefer current task/activity rows for live stage while preserving packet snapshots as warning/source-map evidence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-026, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK012 Are UI state requirements consistent with the API state model, avoiding client-side reinterpretation, synthesis, or override of server-derived states? [Resolved] [Spec §FR-022, Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-037, Plan §UI State Projection Contract]
  - Evidence: `spec.md` FR-037 and `plan.md` §UI State Projection Contract now make API section states authoritative and prohibit client-side reinterpretation, synthesis, upgrade/downgrade, override, coercion, and local stale/completeness inference.

## Scenario Coverage
